smt-2012-algebra-01.title: Symmetry of the parabola
smt-2012-algebra-01.body:
The expression is an upward-opening parabola in $x$, symmetric about $x=3$ (the numbers $1,\dots,5$ are symmetric about $3$), so its minimum is at $x=3$: $4+1+0+1+4=10$.

**Answer: 10**

smt-2012-algebra-01.title: Expand
smt-2012-algebra-01.body:
The sum is $5x^2-30x+55=5(x-3)^2+10$, minimized at $x=3$ with value $10$.

**Answer: 10**

smt-2012-algebra-02.title: Base 1 or exponent 0
smt-2012-algebra-02.body:
The base $\frac15(x^2-10x+26)=\frac15\big((x-5)^2+1\big)$ is always positive. For a positive base $a$, $a^y=1$ holds iff $a=1$ or $y=0$ (if $a\ne1$ then $y\mapsto a^y$ is strictly monotonic).

- Base $=1$: $x^2-10x+21=0$, so $x=3$ or $x=7$.
- Exponent $=0$: $x^2-6x+5=0$, so $x=1$ or $x=5$.

**Answer: $x=1,3,5,7$**

smt-2012-algebra-03.title: Factor and telescope
smt-2012-algebra-03.body:
$\frac{n^3-1}{n^3+1}=\frac{n-1}{n+1}\cdot\frac{n^2+n+1}{n^2-n+1}$.

The first factors telescope: $\prod_{n=2}^{k}\frac{n-1}{n+1}=\frac{1\cdot2}{k(k+1)}$. Since $n^2-n+1=(n-1)^2+(n-1)+1$, the second factors also telescope: $\prod_{n=2}^k\frac{n^2+n+1}{n^2-n+1}=\frac{k^2+k+1}{3}$.

For $k=16$: $\frac{2}{16\cdot17}\cdot\frac{273}{3}=\frac{2\cdot91}{272}=\frac{91}{136}$.

**Answer: $\frac{91}{136}$**

smt-2012-algebra-04.title: Factor
smt-2012-algebra-04.body:
Rearrange: $xyz-2(xy+xz+yz)+4(x+y+z)-8=-1$. The left side is $(x-2)(y-2)(z-2)$. So the product of three integers is $-1$, hence each factor is $\pm1$ with an odd number of $-1$'s.

- All three $-1$: $(x,y,z)=(1,1,1)$.
- Exactly one $-1$: one variable is $1$ and the other two are $3$: $(1,3,3),(3,1,3),(3,3,1)$.

**Answer: $(1,1,1),(1,3,3),(3,1,3),(3,3,1)$**

smt-2012-algebra-05.title: Double roots of P-3
smt-2012-algebra-05.body:
$Q(x)=P(x)-3$ is $0$ at $x=2,3$, and since these are maxima of $P$ (so $Q'=0$ there) they are double roots. Being quartic, $Q(x)=a(x-2)^2(x-3)^2$.

$P(1)=0$ gives $a\cdot1\cdot4+3=0$, so $a=-\frac34$. Then $P(5)=-\frac34\cdot9\cdot4+3=-27+3=-24$.

**Answer: $-24$**

smt-2012-algebra-06.title: Vieta's formulas
smt-2012-algebra-06.body:
For a monic cubic with roots $a,b,c$, $f(0)=-abc$. By Vieta on the given cubic, $\left(a-\frac1b\right)+\left(b-\frac1c\right)+\left(c-\frac1a\right)=5$ and $\left(a-\frac1b\right)\left(b-\frac1c\right)\left(c-\frac1a\right)=-3$.

Expand the product: $\left(a-\frac1b\right)\left(b-\frac1c\right)\left(c-\frac1a\right)=abc-\frac1{abc}-\left[(a+b+c)-\left(\frac1a+\frac1b+\frac1c\right)\right]$, and the bracket is exactly the sum of the three roots, $5$.

So with $t=abc$: $t-\frac1t-5=-3$, i.e. $t^2-2t-1=0$, $t=1\pm\sqrt2$. The two triples correspond to these two values of $abc$.

Hence $f(0)^3+g(0)^3=-(1+\sqrt2)^3-(1-\sqrt2)^3=-\left(2+2\cdot3\cdot2\right)=-14$.

**Answer: $-14$**

smt-2012-algebra-07.title: Only powers of 2 can be exceptions
smt-2012-algebra-07.body:
Zeros of $\sin(ax)$ are $x=t\pi/a$; zeros of $\cos(ax)$ are $x=(t+\frac12)\pi/a$.

Suppose $b=2^m(1+2k)$ with $k\ge1$ is not a power of $2$. Then $2^m<b$ is a zero of some factor $f_i(a_ix)$. If it is $\sin$: $2^ma_i=t\pi$, so $ba_i=(1+2k)t\pi$ is also a zero. If it is $\cos$: $2^ma_i=(t+\frac12)\pi$, so $ba_i=(1+2k)(t+\frac12)\pi=\left(\text{integer}+\frac12\right)\pi$ is a zero as well. Then $f(b)=0$, a contradiction. So $b$ is a power of $2$.

Every power of $2$ up to $2012$ works: for $b=2^m$ use $\prod_{i=1}^m\cos(\pi x/2^i)\cdot\prod_{j=b+1}^{2012}\sin(\pi x/j)$; the cosines kill all integers $x<b$ not equal to... (each $x=2^s(\text{odd})$ with $s<m$ is a zero of $\cos(\pi x/2^{s+1})$), and the sines kill every integer from $b+1$ to $2012$, while $b=2^m$ is not killed by any.

Sum: $1+2+4+\dots+1024=2047$.

**Answer: 2047**

smt-2012-algebra-08.title: A factorization
smt-2012-algebra-08.body:
$(x+y)(y+z)(z+x)=\left(x^2y+y^2z+z^2x\right)+\left(xy^2+yz^2+zx^2\right)+2xyz=-1+5-4=0$. So one of the sums is $0$; by symmetry of the cyclic system say $x=-y$ (the cyclic symmetry makes the three cases equivalent).

Then $xyz=-y^2z=-2$, so $y^2z=2$. The first equation becomes $y^3+y^2z-yz^2=-1$, i.e. $y^3-yz^2=-3=-\frac32y^2z$. Dividing by $y^2z$ and putting $a=y/z$: $a-\frac1a=-\frac32$, i.e. $(2a-1)(a+2)=0$.

- $a=\frac12$: $y=\frac z2$, $y^2z=\frac{z^3}4=2$, $z=2$; then $x+y+z=z=2$.
- $a=-2$: $y=-2z$, $y^2z=4z^3=2$, $z=\sqrt[3]{1/2}$; $x+y+z=z=\sqrt[3]{1/2}$.

Both occur, e.g. $(x,y,z)=(-1,1,2)$ and $(\sqrt[3]4,-\sqrt[3]4,\sqrt[3]{1/2})$, which satisfy all three equations.

**Answer: $2$ or $\sqrt[3]{1/2}$**

smt-2012-algebra-09.title: Complete a square
smt-2012-algebra-09.body:
$4xy=(x+y-z)^2+2(xy+xz+yz)-(x^2+y^2+z^2)\ge0+8-7=1$, so $xy\ge\frac14$.

Equality needs $z=x+y$: then $xy+xz+yz=x^2+3xy+y^2=4$, giving $(x+y)^2=\frac{15}4$, $(x-y)^2=\frac{11}4$ with $xy=\frac14$. Real solution: $x=\frac{\sqrt{15}+\sqrt{11}}4$, $y=\frac{\sqrt{15}-\sqrt{11}}4$, $z=\frac{\sqrt{15}}2$ (check: squares sum to $7$).

**Answer: $\frac14$**

smt-2012-algebra-09.title: AM-GM
smt-2012-algebra-09.body:
$(x+y+z)^2=7+8=15$. Minimizing $xy=4-(x+y)z$ means maximizing $(x+y)z$; WLOG $x+y,z>0$, and AM-GM gives $(x+y)z\le\frac{(x+y+z)^2}4=\frac{15}4$. So $xy\ge4-\frac{15}4=\frac14$.

**Answer: $\frac14$**

smt-2012-algebra-10.title: Parity probabilities and a product
smt-2012-algebra-10.body:
Let $Y_n=\lceil\log_{2n}X_n\rceil$. $Y_n=-k$ iff $(2n)^{-k}<X_n\le(2n)^{-(k-1)}$... precisely $Y_n=-j$ when $(2n)^{-(j+1)}<X_n\le(2n)^{-j}$. $Y_n$ is odd when $j$ is odd: $P=\sum_{k\ge1}\left[(2n)^{-(2k-1)}-(2n)^{-2k}\right]=\frac{\frac1{2n}\left(1-\frac1{2n}\right)}{1-\frac1{(2n)^2}}=\frac{1}{2n+1}$.

Then $E\left[(-1)^{Y_n}\right]=1-\frac2{2n+1}=\frac{2n-1}{2n+1}$. By independence, $E\left[(-1)^{\sum Y_n}\right]=\prod_{n=1}^{2012}\frac{2n-1}{2n+1}=\frac1{4025}$ (telescoping).

If $p$ is the probability that the sum is even, $p-(1-p)=\frac1{4025}$, so $p=\frac{2013}{4025}$.

**Answer: $\frac{2013}{4025}$**
